title: The modern theme lacks some interaction feedback in comparison to the classic theme
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.6-dev3 ### System information Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS ### Issue description Interaction feedback is important. It conveys immediate confirmation to the users' actions and a sense a speed and quality. I noticed that, due to some color generation choices in the modern theme, some of the interaction feedback in this theme is not perceptible, in comparison to the classic theme. I will begin by a bit of theory before explaining the actual bug, because this point can be more or less sucessfully understood by different audiences - speaking by experience. ## Interaction feedback theory IMHO, good interaction feedback should happen in all different steps of a user interaction. Since Godot is mostly interacted with a mouse - although the following is valid using a finger on a touchscreen as well - let's take example of basic interactions. Here is the main point : **A mouse click is not a single discrete event** - it is compound of two : - the button being **pressed**, or down, - and the button being **released**, or up. Those never happen at the exact same time, even if just milliseconds apart. The two events deserve separate feedback. Feedback means to show a confirmation on screen at the exact moment the event occurs by occuring an immediate change in graphics or colors, so that the user can directly make an "action = reaction" haptic association. An interaction event can be the part of a longer chain of events that takes time. Showing timely interaction is crucial even if the event is not fully done yet. For example, if something should change after loading when ticking a checkbox, I find it to be frustrating to feel the checkbox change only after the loading is done. Immediate feedback is basically telling the user "yes, I heard you", even if the task behind requires more time. The way many web interfaces are implemented give a "bad" example of timely interaction feedback. The pressed state is often forgotten, the wait for server-side confirmation before state change can make the things feel slow, and the use of slow fade transitions create an impression of sluggishness. ### Button The button click has three states on normal interaction. **Normal, Hover, Pressed.** **Interaction example for a button** Normal : the button in its idle state Hover : the mouse approaches the button and hovers it Pressed : the user presses and holds the mouse button down Hover (again) : the user releases the mouse button -> **the main button event fires at this moment** Normal : the mouse moves away from the button Eventually, the focus can add up to those, triggered by the button down stage or keyboard focus. ### Two-state element (toggle button, checkbox, menu, dropdown, foldable pane, tabs...) The basic interaction states are still the same: **Normal, Hover, Pressed.** We mix it up with the two states of the togglable element: **Unchecked, Checked, (Transient / Undecided / "third state")** _The third state is very rare but worth mentioning - can be for example reflecting a group selection state of both checked and unchecked items thus not able to determine. We will ignore it for now._ The mix gives those combinations: **Normal, Hover, Pressed, Checked, Hover+Checked, Pressed+Checked.** What does correspond to the checked state? - Checkbox, radio button, toggle button : checked (obviously) - Tab : when this is the currently active tab - Foldable pane : when the pane is unfolded - Dropdown : when the dropdown menu or selector is visible - Menu headers, like the File / Edit... menus of desktop apps : when the corresponding menu is open - **Interaction example for a checkbox** Normal : the checkbox is unchecked Hover : the mouse approaches the button and hovers it Pressed : the user presses and holds the mouse button down Hover + checked : the user releases the mouse button -> **the checkbox becomes checked at this point** Checked : the mouse moves away from the button Hover + checked : the mouse moves back onto the checked checkbox Pressed + checked : the user presses and holds the mouse button down Hover : the user releases the mouse button -> **the checkbox becomes unchecked at this point** Normal : the mouse moves away from the checkbox ### Transitions between states In the two examples above, each transition should be visible on the screen. Else it can feel clunky, slow, unresponding and cause frustration. The item that should show the interaction feedback is the one which is touched directly. For example, not showing a button hover change while assuming that a on-hover tooltip would do the job still feels strange. What can be realistically done is also dependent on the current limitations of the engine. For example, the current implementation of the button in its toggle mode (not the checkbox) locks it in the pressed state when it is checked instead of handling a distinct checked aspect. ## Spots with missing interaction feedback ### Checkboxes The difference between states is barely perceptible. Here, there is no perceptible feedback while pressing the button down on an unchecked checkbox. Same thing when hovering a checked checkbox. This is frustrating. The classic theme shows a better differenciation of hover and pressed state changes. ### Menus No difference between the hover and "menu open" states. The menu header item does not appear to respond itself to the "button down" interaction. Showing hover / "menu open" Mouse down gives no reaction = frustrating. The classic theme shows a difference. ### Bottom buttons No difference between the hover and "palette open" states i.e. button toggled or checked. Showing hover / checked. Mouse down gives no reaction = frustrating. The classic theme shows a difference. ### Tree items The hover color is the same as the selected one. We should be able to tell the difference, with a different opacity for example. Classic theme ### Foldable sections in inspector No feedback on hover. Showing normal / hover. The classic theme shows a hover feedback. ### Dropdown lists in inspector Missing feedback when open. Showing normal / hover / open. Classic theme This is due to the nature of the "flat" buttons that only rely on the text color. The focus rectangle has been removed on click as well and served as some sort of click feedback until then. ## Takeaways This can be fixed by some fine-tuning in the points I mentioned. Making proper interaction feedback goes a long way in the quality feeling of the editor! ### Steps to reproduce Create an empty project. Play around with the elements I mentioned. Swap between the Classic and Modern themes to feel the difference (I insist on "feel"). ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
